checks.description: Collector output persisted to local files and read back (every line parses as OTLP JSON)
Spans received from every application service
All trace IDs (32 hex) and span IDs (16 hex) are valid, non-zero and unique
Every trace ID returned to the smoke client is present in the exported traces
Each smoke trace is one tree: a single gateway SERVER root, every parent present
Trace context propagates across service boundaries: every order trace contains gateway->inventory, gateway->order, order->inventory and order->payment (CLIENT span parent of the callee's SERVER span)
Database calls appear as postgresql CLIENT spans inside order and inventory, parented within the same service
Service identity is consistent: each service has exactly one instance id, only known service names appear, and SERVER spans carry that service's own routes
Log records received from every application service (OTLP) and from postgres (Docker fluentd driver)
Application logs are structured (severity, timestamp, message, typed attributes); postgres lines arrive in a structured envelope (container identity, timestamp) with a plain-text body

checks.description: Logs correlate to traces: every smoke trace has logs from each service in it, and each log's (trace_id, span_id) resolves to a span of the same service whose time window contains the log timestamp
Postgres logged the connections opened by the order and inventory pools during the smoke window (matched by application_name)

inventory: 2026-10-12 04:49:05.203 UTC [121] shop@shopLOG:  connection authorized: user=shop database=shop application_name=inventory

checks.description: Every service exports request count, latency histogram (app and HTTP semconv) and process CPU/memory metrics
Request counters equal the requests the smoke client actually made, per service, route, method and status
Latency histograms are consistent: per-series count equals the request counter, sums are positive, and the OTel HTTP semconv histogram agrees
Error counters reflect reality: gateway counted exactly the expected client rejection(s); no server errors anywhere
Container resource metrics (docker_stats: CPU, memory, network) for every service and postgres during the smoke window
Nothing lost between collector and disk: records read back from the files equal the counts the file exporters report as sent
Collector self-metrics: OTLP, fluent_forward and docker_stats receivers accepted data, file exporters sent it, nothing was refused or failed

Timestamps are consistent: start <= end for all spans, smoke spans fall inside the client's request window (host/VM slack 500 ms), children nest in parents (1 ms slack), metric points have start <= time
Service identity is the same across signals: each service reports one service.instance.id, identical in its traces, logs and metrics
No unexpected service errors: no ERROR-status spans, no 5xx server spans, no ERROR logs; every WARN log belongs to the deliberately rejected request
